[RTIM.14.7] **Oracle check.** The interpreter observes the engine's stream events
and final working memory and checks every `Oracle*` atom over the whole run — `POS`
requires ≥ 1 occurrence, `NEVER` requires 0 ([LTSL.8.3]) — matching by partial
(subset) equality or, on an `OracleEmit` that carries
`has_where`, by the `where` predicate in its place ([LTSL.8.4]). The
predicate is evaluated by a **compiler-synthesized oracle rule matched by the real
engine** ([RTIM.14.11]), never a shadow or parallel evaluator ([RTIM.14.8]): the
rule's LHS is `<schema> <binding> where <pred>`, and the interpreter binds the
`OracleEmit` to that rule by the deterministic name convention. A `where` match
is a firing of that oracle rule on a fact that was **emitted** this
run — the interpreter attributes each firing to an `ACTION_EMIT`
by fact identity (the matched fact handle on the pre-fire event); a firing on an
input / arrange fact that merely satisfies the predicate is **not** a match. The
oracle rule's own effects are not part of the observed output. v1 exact-value
makes a float match exact ([LDET.3.2]).

An `OracleEmit` that carries both `has_where` and a `slot_match`, and an
`OraclePublish` that carries `has_where`, are ones no conforming compiler writes
([LTSL.8.4]). The interpreter **must** fail the case and name the atom, as it fails an assertion
it does not understand ([RTIM.14.9]), and **must not** check either half alone.
